title: FlashPro
author: Rodrigo Vargas (Stern '17)
geography: San Francisco-based; US and international sales; Argentina, Japan, Australia and Sweden expansion options
prompt: Your client is FlashPro Inc., a San Francisco based technology company that develops and sells wearable and mountable action cameras. FlashPro's CEO believes that the company's growth has stagnated and has hired your firm to remedy that issue.

clarifying_info.answer: FlashPro is public and sells in the United States and internationally. Its main product, CamPro, is a mounted camera primarily used for action sports, recently also used for other recreation.
Manufacturing is outsourced to contractors in China. Sales channels are distributors, retail and FlashPro's website.
The industry is highly competitive and customers are very loyal to brands.
Only when specifically asked: camera price is $250 and gross margin has remained at 50%. These trends are expected to continue in 2018.
Only when specifically asked: 60% of camera sales have been in the US over the last five years, with a similar split expected in 2018; the rest are international.

interviewer_notes: Test the ability to synthesize several exhibits, focus on profitability drivers and brainstorm revenue/profit growth creatively. Begin with a market and profitability framework, including COGS, R&D, G&A and sales/marketing. Give Exhibits 1–3 for the gross-profit question, but release price, margin and geographic mix on request. Encourage organized growth alternatives; steer toward new geographies if needed and then show Exhibit 4. Entry analysis is deliberately incomplete: channel-margin advantages are hypotheses, not quantified profitability, and entry costs and competitive responses have not been supplied.

suggested_framework.summary: Diagnose market and profit drivers, then compare ways to grow the existing business and enter new markets.

children.label: Revenue: market size, penetration, share and price
Product attributes, channels, pricing and advertising

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you diagnose FlashPro's growth issue?
stages.release_when: Read the prompt and give background clarifications on request.
stages.info_to_release: FlashPro is a public US and international seller of CamPro action cameras, outsources manufacturing to China, and sells through distributors, retailers and its website. The industry is highly competitive with strong brand loyalty.
stages.expected_answer: Separate market growth, penetration, FlashPro share and price from the cost structure. Assess competitors, customers, substitutes and suppliers. Include COGS, R&D, G&A and sales/marketing in the broader profitability tree; then explore existing-product and new-market growth.
good_answer_signals: Avoids treating a revenue-growth concern as automatically a cost problem.
Builds a clear revenue and profit driver tree.

stages.interviewer_asks: What is FlashPro's expected gross profit for 2018?
stages.release_when: Hand out Exhibits 1–3. Give the price, margin and geographic sales split only when asked.
stages.info_to_release: 2018 potential US market is 16,000 thousand customers with 85% penetration. FlashPro has 30% share, steady for five years and the same in the US and worldwide. On request: $250 camera price, 50% gross margin, and 60% US/40% international sales mix continuing in 2018. FlashPro alone offers wearables.
stages.expected_answer: US revenue = 16 million × 85% × 30% × $250 = $1.02 billion. International revenue = $1.02 billion × 40% / 60% = $680 million. Total revenue is $1.7 billion. COGS at 50% are $850 million, so gross profit is $850 million. Do not mistake the exhibit's thousands of customers for individual customers or treat US revenue as global revenue.
good_answer_signals: Triangulates market size, penetration, share, price and geography.
Keeps units explicit and distinguishes gross from net profit.

stages.interviewer_asks: What are the current revenue-growth prospects, holding other factors constant, and what alternatives could boost the top line?
stages.release_when: After the gross-profit calculation; use the first three exhibits before introducing expansion data.
stages.info_to_release: The US potential market is forecast to rise from 16 million in 2018 to 16.5 million in 2019 and 16.7 million in 2020; penetration rises from 85% to 90% and 95%. Market shares have been steady for five years in a competitive, brand-loyal industry.
stages.expected_answer: Some growth remains, but the potential market's expansion is slowing and penetration approaches saturation. Fierce competition makes share gains difficult. Organize alternatives around the marketing mix (product attributes, channels, price, advertising) and new markets (new products and geographies), considering organic development and M&A. Do not equate slowing growth with a shrinking market or assume a share gain without evidence.
good_answer_signals: Uses the exhibit trends rather than an unstructured idea list.
Explores multiple routes to growth before choosing geography.

stages.interviewer_asks: Which country is most attractive economically, and what should FlashPro consider before entering?
stages.release_when: Provide Exhibit 4 when geographic expansion is raised; steer toward it if necessary.
stages.info_to_release: Current country camera revenues, in USD thousands: Argentina 2,500, Japan 3,500, Australia 3,500, Sweden 2,500. Expected Year 1 shares: 35%, 25%, 20%, 25%; annual market growth for the next three years: 10%, 5%, 10%, 15%. Website mix is 50% in Argentina/Australia and 10% in Japan/Sweden. After Year 3 all markets grow at 5%. No channel margins or entry costs are supplied.
stages.expected_answer: Using the source's convention of three growth periods from the current market and holding the given share constant, Year 3 revenue is Argentina $1,164,625; Japan $1,012,921.875; Australia $931,700; Sweden $950,546.875. Rounded to USD thousands these are 1,165, 1,013, 932 and 951, matching the book. Argentina has the highest projected revenue and a 50% website mix that may improve margins by avoiding intermediaries. Australia has the same website mix but lower revenue. Investigate customers, local competition, regulation, macroeconomic/geopolitical conditions and logistics. Revenue and channel mix alone do not establish investment returns.
good_answer_signals: Compounds growth rather than adding percentages.
Treats channel-margin superiority as an assumption to verify.

stages.interviewer_asks: What is your recommendation and what should the client do next?
stages.release_when: After the country comparison and entry considerations.
stages.expected_answer: Pursue geographic expansion and prioritize further diligence on Argentina: it has the highest modeled Year 3 revenue, about $1.165 million, a 35% assumed share and a 50% website mix. This is a preliminary screen, not a final investment approval. Validate aggressive market-share assumptions, entry costs, channel economics and competitor response. Research Argentina further, assess internal expansion capabilities and plan advertising, channels, promotion and pricing.
good_answer_signals: Connects expansion to limited domestic growth and competition.
Acknowledges omitted costs and the ambitious share assumption.
Does not confuse the small printed expansion-market scale with global revenue.

math.question: What are 2018 US, international and total revenues?
math.answer: $1.7 billion worldwide revenue, comprising $1.02 billion US and $680 million international.

math.question: What is expected 2018 gross profit?
givens: Gross margin 50%, equivalent to COGS of 50% of sales
math.answer: $850 million gross profit; operating expenses have not been deducted.

math.question: Which expansion country has the highest Year 3 revenue?
givens: Current markets in USD: Argentina 2,500,000; Japan 3,500,000; Australia 3,500,000; Sweden 2,500,000
Source solution compounds three years from current market size and holds the stated Year 1 share constant
steps: Rounded USD thousands: Argentina 1,165; Japan 1,013; Australia 932; Sweden 951.
math.answer: Argentina leads with $1,164,625 Year 3 revenue, approximately $1.165 million.

synthesis: Pursue geographic growth and prioritize Argentina for further research. FlashPro's projected 2018 gross profit is $850 million, but slowing US market growth, near-saturation penetration and stable competitive shares limit the domestic runway. Argentina leads the supplied expansion options at approximately $1.165 million in Year 3 revenue and has a 50% direct-website mix that could support higher margins. Validate market shares, entry costs, channel profitability and competitive reactions before approval; assess internal capabilities and develop the marketing and channel plan.
what_great_looks_like: Combines all three initial exhibits with requested commercial inputs.
Keeps customer and dollar-thousands units consistent.
Structures a broad growth brainstorm before country selection.
Recognizes possible channel-margin differences without inventing margins.
Acknowledges that market-entry economics remain incomplete.
common_pitfalls: Treating US revenue as all global revenue.
Dropping the thousands multiplier on customer or country-revenue inputs.
Confusing gross profit with net profit.
Applying simple rather than compound growth.
Assuming the largest current market is the best entry choice.
Treating revenue ranking as a complete investment appraisal.

extraction.notes: All recomputed math matches the book, allowing its rounding to USD thousands. Country-market figures are explicitly in thousands, so Argentina's Year 3 revenue is about $1.165 million, not billion; the unusual scale relative to existing worldwide revenue is preserved rather than repaired. The solution implicitly keeps Year 1 share constant and compounds three growth periods from current market size; this convention is made explicit. Website margins are hypothesized to be higher, not supplied numeric facts. No entry-cost or net-profit result is invented. Candidate exhibit pages 258–261 are clean and fully legible. Difficulty uses max(9,7), Python round(9/2) = 4. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-10-04.
